pull.title: test, refactor: extract script template helpers and expand sigop coverage
pull.body:
**Problem:** The existing sigop-counting paths have thin feature-test coverage, especially around malformed `PUSHDATA` encodings and known-template sigop totals.
The existing code also repeats byte-level template checks in several places, and names like `MAX_OPCODE` / `HasValidOps()` do not make it clear that `scriptPubKey` and `scriptSig` validation only accepts pre-Taproot opcodes.
The combined deserialize + check-block benchmark also makes it hard to measure legacy sigop counting separately.

**Fix:** Add focused coverage for `CountSigOps`, malformed push encodings, common script templates, and fuzz targets that construct standard `scriptPubKeys`.
Extract cheap inline helpers for common script templates, split P2SH sigop counting from plain script sigop counting, and rename the pre-Taproot opcode validity helpers so their scope is explicit.
Add a separate `SigOpsBlock` benchmark so deserialization + hashing, validation, and sigop counting can be measured independently.
The consensus and policy call sites remain behavior-neutral: they perform the same checks as before, through clearer helper functions.

**Follow-up:** These helper refactors are intended to make follow-up optimizations such as #32532 easier to review, because those patches can reuse shared template predicates instead of repeating byte checks.

refactor: split off `P2SH` from `GetSigOpCount`

Move P2SH redeemScript sigop counting into `CountP2SHSigOps` so `CountSigOps` only counts the script it is called on.
The new name mirrors `CountWitnessSigOps`, and taking both `scriptSig` and `scriptPubKey` makes consensus and policy call sites handle P2SH and non-P2SH inputs uniformly.

This also makes `CheckSigopsBIP54` match the BIP54 specification more directly: count sigops in the input `scriptSig`, the previous output's `scriptPubKey`, and the P2SH redeemScript when present.

re: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/32729#discussion_r2258271345

> Why is the _wrapped_-property worth calling out in a P2SH context? Do you mean in contrast to bare multisig? 

Good point. By wrapped scripts I just meant redeemScripts and witnessScripts, but that term was confusing. I think a better version of this is probably:

```c++
/**
 * Count the number of signature operations (sigops) in this script.
 *
 * The `fAccurate` parameter controls how `CHECKMULTISIG` operations are counted.
 * When enforcing the `MAX_BLOCK_SIGOPS_COST` limit, set `fAccurate` to `true` when
 * counting a redeemScript (P2SH) or witnessScript (P2WSH), and set it to `false`
 * when counting a scriptPubKey or scriptSig.
 *
 * Historical note: before P2SH (v0.6), `CHECKMULTISIG` was always counted as
 * MAX_PUBKEYS_PER_MULTISIG (=20), regardless of the actual number of pubkeys.
 * Starting with P2SH — and similarly for P2WSH later — `CHECKMULTISIG` inside
 * the redeemScript/witnessScript began to be counted precisely, using the
 * preceding OP_N to determine the number of pubkeys.
 */
unsigned int CountSigOps(bool fAccurate) const;
```

which cleans up the comment and mentions witness scripts explicitly in the "historical" section.
